feature: Independent backend relevance populations preserve legacy History results

scenarios.name: A different backend's top score cannot demote eligible Apple passages
scenarios.given: Apple-only history already has an eligible Related conversation and Ask passage under unchanged default parameters and global Related/Ask output caps are nonbinding
scenarios.when: an unrelated conversation from an explicitly separate optional relevance group has a higher raw cosine
scenarios.then: the same Apple conversation and Ask passage remain eligible when output caps are nonbinding, without changing any cutoff or claiming the optional match is relevant

scenarios.name: A different backend's score population cannot change Apple's relevance mean
scenarios.given: Apple-only history already has an eligible Related conversation and Ask passage under unchanged default parameters
scenarios.when: many unrelated conversations from an explicitly separate optional relevance group raise the other backend's average score without exceeding the Apple top score
scenarios.then: the original Apple Related and Ask memberships remain unchanged, with global output caps nonbinding for those eligible candidates

scenarios.name: Existing embedders retain one legacy relevance population
scenarios.given: an existing embedder provides multiple Apple language model tags and declares no independent relevance groups
scenarios.when: History searches and retrieves its indexed conversations
scenarios.then: the established single-population floor, mean and top-margin decisions stay unchanged; this is adopted compatibility coverage, not a new historical red

scenarios.name: Cross-group order is independent of incomparable score scales
scenarios.given: two independently admitted relevance groups have identical within-group membership and rank, and global output caps are nonbinding
scenarios.when: only the optional group raw similarity scale changes between two values that both satisfy its unchanged admission rules
scenarios.then: combined Related and Ask conversation order stays the same because group ranks, not cross-group raw cosine magnitudes, determine fusion

scenarios.name: Native optional runtime preserves the fallback search population
scenarios.given: the real native optional model is installed beside a controlled fallback whose existing conversation qualifies by meaning
scenarios.when: many optional-model passages are indexed and the user searches or asks the same question with output caps nonbinding
scenarios.then: the fallback Related result and unchanged Ask passage remain eligible, with separate native runtime and delegated fallback relevance groups; controlled fallback scores do not prove Apple model quality

scenarios.name: Tied multi-group passages have deterministic ranks
scenarios.given: multiple admitted relevance groups include two passages tied in score, date and ordinal, with output caps nonbinding
scenarios.when: the same archive is supplied in opposite tied-record input orders
scenarios.then: multi-group Related and Ask orders remain identical using stable passage identity, while single legacy-group tie behavior stays unchanged
